findings.summary: Candidate 7 left the review-state lines at round 6. The HS53 README status says 'independent contract review, round 6 ... candidate 6 answers rounds 1 to 5', although it now carries the round-6 table and candidate 7's changes. The v5 README status (architecture/seccomp-allowlists-v5/README.md:3) still says 'round 6'. HS53 REVIEW_BRIEF item 8 (line 56) still asks for 'Rounds 1 to 5 ... the README's last five tables ... review-round1 to review-round5', which leaves round 6 out. The v5 brief's item 7 was updated to 'Rounds 1 to 6'.
findings.evidence: git show 08355e02 / 065c4ca4 / ab83c9c0 of these three lines: each earlier candidate moved them on (round 5 -> round 6, 'candidate 5 answers rounds 1 to 4' -> 'candidate 6 answers rounds 1 to 5', brief 'Rounds 1 to 4' -> 'Rounds 1 to 5'). git diff 065c4ca4 ab83c9c0 changes only the title line of each brief and no README status line. The repository's convention (architecture/selinux-matrix-v3/status.json readmeStatusNote) is that a README 'keeps its reviewed ... line; adoption is recorded' elsewhere, and HS53 and v5 have no status file of their own. As published, these lines would misstate the record's review state for good. Fix: 'round 7', 'candidate 7 answers rounds 1 to 6', and brief item 8 'Rounds 1 to 6 ... last six tables ... review-round6'.

findings.summary: H1's AF_UNIX limit says SELinux limits 'which socket files the observer may create (planeon_observer_sock_t)'. The same wording is at spec :449, README :85-88 and v5 README :42-44. In matrix v5's data this holds only among the matrix's own types. For undeclared types it rests on W03's policy module, and no obligation binds that. The connector limit (connectto) does hold in data.
findings.evidence: scripts/selinux_matrix_v3.py allowed(matrix v5, ENROLLED_SEALED, planeon_observer_t, target, sock_file, create): True on planeon_observer_sock_t; False on planeon_i05_sock_t, planeon_broker_sock_t and planeon_run_t (so a missing W03 label rule fails safe, as stated); None (outside the matrix) on tmp_t and var_run_t. Matrix v5 README:163-166 leaves 'ordinary access to undeclared types' to the W03 module. unix_stream_socket connectto on planeon_observer_t is True only for planeon_server_t: False for the broker, the gate, init_t, planeon_admin_t and an undeclared domain. So no other domain can connect to any socket the observer binds (an abstract-namespace bind creates no file at all), and nothing is unsafe. Advice: say 'among planeon socket-file types', or add to O-W03-OBSERVER-UNIT and O-T04-HS53 that the observer gets no sock_file create outside planeon_observer_sock_t.

findings.summary: The replacement for the guide's producer sentences (spec :755) drops the producer's duty to meet 'the native tests below'. Its list of what stays unchanged ('protocol, path, modes, framing, limits and peer checks') does not name the guide's native follow-up.
findings.evidence: The quoted text ends 'An operator must supply an open-source, reviewed implementation meeting this protocol and the native tests below.' The replacement reads '... not an operator-supplied implementation; ... The guide's protocol, path, modes, framing, limits and peer checks are unchanged'. The guide's 'Source acceptance and native follow-up' section (docs/alpha-2/POLICY_OBSERVATION_READINESS.md:165-185: peer spoofing, FD injection, process replacement, observer restart/loss, absent producer ...) is not quoted, so it stays in force. But neither O-R10-HE004-I01 nor O-T04-HS53 restates it for HE-004-I01. Advice: add 'and native follow-up' to the unchanged list, or say that HE-004-I01 meets this protocol and the guide's native tests.
